title: Mirzapur The Movie Crosses $2 Million In North America, Climbing Indian Box Office Charts
excerpt: The crime thriller took ₹9.5 crore on its second Friday to reach ₹163.27 crore net in India, overtaking Awarapan 2 for the year's No. 6 spot, while its $2.05 million North American haul made it the fourth Bollywood film of 2026 to cross $2 million in the territory.
body:
• Mirzapur The Movie collected ₹9.5 crore net at the Indian box office on its second Friday (day 8), taking its 8-day domestic net total to ₹163.27 crore, according to Koimoi's estimates.
  • The crime thriller overtook Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 (₹156.04 crore) to become Bollywood's 6th highest-grossing film of 2026 in India.
  • In North America, the film crossed $2 million in its first week ($2.05 million / ₹19.59 crore), the 4th Bollywood film of 2026 to do so, and is closing in on Bhooth Bangla ($2.3 million) for 3rd place.
  • With ₹230.66 crore worldwide in 8 days against a reported ₹90 crore budget, the film is on track to enter the ₹200 crore net club in India.

Mirzapur The Movie is enjoying a second week most films only dream of. The big-screen adaptation of Amazon's hit crime series collected ₹9.5 crore net at the Indian box office on its second Friday — its eighth day in theaters — dropping just 9.95% from its first Thursday's ₹10.55 crore, pushing its domestic total to ₹163.27 crore net, according to Koimoi's box office estimates. The haul pushes it past Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 (₹156.04 crore), making it the sixth highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2026 in India. Overseas, the film crossed the $2 million mark in its first week in North America, the fourth Bollywood release of the year to do so.

Context & Background

The film arrives with one of the strongest built-in audiences in recent Bollywood history. The Mirzapur web series, which ran for multiple seasons on Prime Video, gave the theatrical adaptation genuine pre-release buzz in India and among the diaspora. Directed by Gurmmeet Singh and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar under Excel Entertainment and Amazon MGM Studios, it stars Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Divyenndu, Jitendra Kumar, and Ravi Kishan, with a reported ₹90 crore budget.

That IP advantage meant one of the strongest openings of the year: ₹153.77 crore net in week one, and a day-8 hold that signals unusually strong audience reception. Overseas it grossed over ₹35 crore in its first week, taking the worldwide tally to ₹230.66 crore gross in 8 days.

Impact & Analysis

The day-8 milestone redraws the 2026 Bollywood leaderboard. With 163.27 crore net, Mirzapur The Movie sits sixth among Bollywood's 2026 grossers in India — ahead of Awarapan 2 (156.04 crore), Welcome To The Jungle (137.93 crore), and Cocktail 2 (104.53 crore). Above it: Hanuman Ansh (173.63 crore), Dhamaal 4 (177.92 crore), and Bhooth Bangla (199.23 crore), with Border 2 (362.76 crore) and Dhurandhar 2 (1186.32 crore) at the top.

The ₹200 crore net milestone looks days away, with Dhamaal 4 and Bhooth Bangla within reach in its lifetime run. At a reported ₹90 crore budget, the film has been in the black for days.

"With such momentum and no threat from Haiwaan, the film will comfortably enter the 200 crore club (net) in the coming days."

— Koimoi, box office report

Diaspora Angle

It opened in the US and Canada with $314K on day one and finished its first week at $2.05 million — about ₹19.59 crore. That makes it the fourth Bollywood film of 2026 to cross the $2 million mark in the territory, now chasing Bhooth Bangla ($2.3 million) for third place on the year's North America chart, led by Dhurandhar 2 ($28.64 million) and Border 2 ($3.5 million).

The series' diaspora fanbase did the heavy lifting: one of the most engaged NRI followings of any Indian IP, converting directly into opening-weekend turnout across North American theaters — a market where the film faced none of the show-count pressure it saw in India.

"Mirzapur The Movie's grand success isn't limited to the domestic market, as the 'Bhaukaal' could be seen internationally as well."

— Koimoi, box office report

What's Next

The next markers are clear. In India, the ₹200 crore net milestone is days away, and the second weekend will decide whether the film can chase down Dhamaal 4 and Bhooth Bangla for a higher finish. Much depends on screen allocation against Haiwaan's first full week and Hanuman Ansh's continued surge.

In North America, the chase for Bhooth Bangla's $2.3 million comes down to the hold — the film needs roughly $250K more in the territory to claim the year's third spot. Either way, Mirzapur The Movie has delivered the year's clearest lesson for Bollywood studios: an established series IP with a loyal diaspora following converts directly into theatrical dollars, and the ceiling for such adaptations keeps rising.
